vulnerability_patterns.description: A lookahead array access reads past the end of the input buffer when the loop index reaches the last valid element and the condition still evaluates the next element.
trigger_conditions: Loop variable `a` iterates with condition `a < length`, so the final iteration allows `a == length-1`
Current byte `ch` is loaded from `Data[a]` and equals `\r` on that final iteration
The code then evaluates `Data[a+1]` without first proving `a+1 < length`
fix_patterns: Add an explicit upper-bound guard `a < length-1` before evaluating the lookahead access `Data[a+1]`
Keep the dangerous sink unchanged but place a short-circuit barrier in the same condition so the out-of-bounds read is never evaluated
evidence_lines: New guarded condition: `if (ch == '\r' && a < length-1 && Data[a+1] == '\n') continue;`

shared_analysis.analysis_rationale: The patch changes a direct lookahead read `Data[a+1]` inside the loop body to a guarded read `a < length-1 && Data[a+1] == '\n'`. In the old code, the loop permits `a == length-1`, so when `ch == '\r'` on the last iteration it evaluates `Data[a+1]`, reading one byte past the valid range. The fix is a patch-local bounds barrier placed on the exact expression that performed the dangerous access.
